content: This is some good advice on working with a Dot (I will never stop capitalizing it, OpenAI!) but also a sign of the issues with the UX of Dot (& all personal agents) right now: you can't easily tell what they are working on, what they know about you, and what they will do for you https://x.com/i/article/2116298153058037760
Magic doesn't always need to be the default mode of an AI system. Control is nice, especially for a personal assistant.
Lame will walk, blind will see, and poor will have good news announced to them.
If you are early, but execution is so hard and it takes so long that it becomes moot by the time it's accomplished, you might as well have been late.

I don't believe that ANY of those companies will exist in 5 years in their current form. Tech will live, but containers in which it had sprung will be cast away. Within 5 years, Google, SpaceX, Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic will all likely be worth $10T+. Sure, 25% of that might come from inflation... but it's not a good time to bet against tech while we're in the middle of a literal revolution.
Huh Interesting how Kimi has a near-identical personality to Astra...
For reference, the big proprietary models look very different from each other. (And not every open model overlaps so much with a closed one)

Agree with this. Scheduled local Codex sessions that email you or message you offer a lot more control over important tasks because you can change the context and prompts. I still enjoy using a Dot for many tasks, but it is not a replacement. https://x.com/krishnanrohit/status/2116323804695966093?a=A_RcI2tdDKt_VYbF3y4&s=20 @emollick For many of the use cases, I've gone back to starting to use Codex locally precisely because of this. I know when I can and should intervene.
